open_points.subject: A01 canonical-number admission
open_points.text: “an integer spelling that an IEEE double neither holds exactly nor writes as its shortest round-trip form … is refused”
open_points.question: What happens when an integer spelling satisfies only one of those conditions—for example, it is not held exactly but is nevertheless the double’s shortest round-trip spelling?
options: Refuse every integer whose mathematical value is not represented exactly
Refuse only when both exact representation and shortest-spelling equality fail
Accept every number JCS can serialize, using the parsed IEEE-double value
open_points.default_guess: Refuse every integer whose mathematical value is not represented exactly.

open_points.subject: A01 integral and fractional canonical values
open_points.text: “An integral JSON value has no insignificant fractional zero in its canonical bytes, a fractional value keeps its significant fraction”
open_points.question: Are “integral” and “fractional” determined from the source spelling, its exact mathematical value, or the parsed IEEE-double value, particularly for `1.0`, `1e0`, `-0.0`, or a fractional spelling rounded by IEEE conversion to an integer?
options: Classify the exact mathematical value expressed by the source text and refuse conversion that loses a significant fraction
Classify the parsed IEEE-double value and canonicalise it according to JCS
Classify lexically by whether the source token contains a fraction or exponent
open_points.default_guess: Classify the parsed IEEE-double value and canonicalise it according to JCS.

open_points.subject: A16 request canonicalisation and schema validation
open_points.text: “A request whose strict request model has integer fields accepts JSON integers after the surface canonicalises its arguments” versus rule 1, where the request “fits that operation's schema” before canonical form is kept only for “every JSON text it carries as a string”
open_points.question: Does the surface canonicalise the whole request’s ordinary arguments before strict operation-schema validation, or only canonicalise embedded JSON texts after the request schema has already been validated?
options: Parse and canonicalise all request arguments before strict operation-schema validation
Validate the ordinary request model first and canonicalise only embedded JSON-text string fields afterward
Validate integer tokens separately without canonicalising the whole request
open_points.default_guess: Parse the request while preserving numeric meaning, validate its strict model, and canonicalise only values that the rules explicitly require to be retained canonically.

open_points.subject: A16 integer request fields
open_points.text: “accepts JSON integers after the surface canonicalises its arguments; canonicalisation does not turn them into fractional JSON numbers”
open_points.question: Which accepted numeric spellings count as integers for a strict integer field after canonicalisation: only integer-token spellings, or every accepted number whose canonical or mathematical value is integral, including `1.0`, `1e3`, `-0`, and large exponent-form values?
options: Only source tokens with no fraction or exponent
Any accepted value whose exact mathematical value is integral
Any accepted value whose parsed IEEE-double value is integral
Only values within JavaScript’s safe-integer range
open_points.default_guess: Accept any A01-admitted value whose parsed IEEE-double value is integral, subject to the field’s own bounds.
